prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules recruit ubiquitin ligases to destroy chosen proteins, through the PROTAC concept and the identification of cereblon as the target of molecular glue degraders

statement.case_for: I have moved from B044 to B020 as the single prize part. Round 1 showed that my own proposal has no explicit support from any other member and that the novelty objection to it (the 2010 cross-coupling prize) is shared by the people who respect its maturity most. Targeted protein degradation is a different kind of chemical idea: a designed small molecule forms a ternary complex that is productive only because of the geometry and cooperativity between ligase and target, so catalytic, event-driven removal replaces occupancy-based inhibition. As a synthetic chemist I find the chemistry real and not merely pharmacological, since linker design, ligase ligand design and ternary-complex cooperativity are molecular design problems with transferable rules. It has been confirmed by structures and by many independent groups. Crews and Deshaies supply the concept, and Handa's identification of cereblon explains how thalidomide-type glues work, so both strands rest on the same mechanism and one citation can state a principle rather than list compounds.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC drug is approved, and I still regard that as the main residual risk: if clinical results disappoint, a prize for a young modality would look early. The three-person limit omits Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim and Ito, each with a credible claim, and the PROTAC and glue lineages are historically separate, so the citation can be read as a compromise. The Medicine committee could also argue the achievement as pharmacology. If the committee prefers a mature synthetic method with clean attribution, B044 (Buchwald, Hartwig) remains the stronger answer on maturity and priority clarity, though weaker on novelty relative to 2010 and complicated by Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work.

responses.point: You asked whether the committee can justify a second cross-coupling prize while a new modality remains unrecognised, and whether B020 can be worded as one principle.
responses.response: I cannot give a strong justification for a second cross-coupling prize ahead of degraders, and your question is the reason I changed my position. The ligand-design logic behind C-N coupling is genuine, but the committee would be rewarding an extension of a principle already honoured in 2010, with Kosugi's tin-amide aminations making priority less tidy than I first presented. On wording, I accept your formulation: the shared ternary-complex mechanism lets one citation cover the PROTAC concept and cereblon identification without implying that Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto, Kim or Ito did not contribute. I would keep the citation on the principle and not on named compounds.

responses.point: Induced proximity is a different mode of action altogether, and B044 could be considered later but not ahead of B020.
responses.response: I agree with the ordering and with your point that C-N coupling is an extension of the 2010 logic with very large practical impact. I now give more weight to mode of action than to years of use. Your physical-chemistry framing (cooperativity, linker design, interfacial protein-protein recognition) persuades me that the chemistry of ternary complexes is established enough to be the basis of a prize, even though I would have asked for more clinical evidence a round ago. I would still note that B044 should not be forgotten if B020 attribution fails.

responses.point: You chose Ciulli as the third name and a bifunctional-only citation, arguing that structure-based VHL ligands and ternary-complex work turned PROTACs into a design discipline.
responses.response: Ciulli's contribution is the strongest rival for the third seat and I do not dismiss it. I still prefer Handa, because the cereblon identification is the single discovery that converts the thalidomide history into a mechanistically understood class, and a bifunctional-only citation would leave the glue strand, which four members want covered, outside the prize. Your design-discipline argument is the reason I accept the maturity of the field. If the committee wants a bifunctional-only citation, I would accept Ciulli in place of Handa, but then the citation must not suggest that glues are part of the achievement.

responses.point: You propose B047 (Liu alone) as a second part together with Crews and Deshaies for B020, and treat base editing as a chemical principle distinct from CRISPR.
responses.response: I agree that the adenine deaminase evolved to act on DNA is real molecular design and that Liu alone is the defensible attribution. I do not support adding it now: the 2020 prize for programmable nucleases is close, the Kondo and Nishida cytidine-deamination priority question is unresolved, and clinical use is young. A two-part prize would also drop Handa from the three-person limit, which I think weakens the B020 citation. I keep B047 as an alternative for a later year or if the committee insists on a second part.

responses.point: B020 might be claimed as Medicine, and the combined PROTAC-glue citation may look like a forced merger of two lineages.
responses.response: I share both worries but consider them answerable. The chemical content of the achievement, small-molecule-induced ligase-target proximity and its design rules, is the part that belongs in Chemistry, and the citation should say so. On the merger, the shared mechanism is stated in the citation wording, so it describes one principle. You pressed me on prematurity in round 1, and I now think conceptual and mechanistic maturity, independently confirmed, is the correct criterion, with clinical approval a reason for caution but not disqualification.

uncertainties: Whether the missing approved PROTAC drug should still lead the committee to delay B020; I now see it as tolerable but not negligible.
Whether Handa or Ciulli takes the third seat, and whether the citation may fairly span both strands without reading as a compromise.
Priority dates for the 2001 PROTAC work and the 2010 cereblon identification come from general knowledge and have not been checked in this process.
If B020 attribution cannot be agreed, whether B044 with a clear statement on Kosugi would be accepted as a fallback.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict with any shortlisted candidate is apparent from my profile: I have no documented tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa, Ciulli, Buchwald, Hartwig, Liu or other shortlisted names, and my mentor Masamune and my former institutions do not appear on the shortlist. I sit on the committee with Lund colleagues Linke and Sparr, which is not a recusal issue. No change to my earlier disclosure.
